neighbourhoods.name: Kettering
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian terraces from the boot and shoe era near the centre, with post-war and large new-build estates such as Hanwood Park.

neighbourhoods.name: Corby
neighbourhoods.housing: New-town estates of the 1950s to 1970s built for the steelworks, with large new-build areas such as Priors Hall.

neighbourhoods.name: Wellingborough
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian terraces near the town centre, post-war estates and new-build homes at Stanton Cross.

neighbourhoods.name: Rushden
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian and Edwardian terraces from the shoe industry and later estates.

neighbourhoods.name: Raunds and Irthlingborough
neighbourhoods.housing: Small towns of stone and brick terraces, with post-war and modern estates.

neighbourhoods.name: Desborough and Rothwell
neighbourhoods.housing: Ironstone and brick terraces in the old centres and new estates on the edges.

neighbourhoods.name: Oundle
neighbourhoods.housing: A limestone market town of Georgian and older houses, many listed.

neighbourhoods.name: Thrapston
neighbourhoods.housing: A Nene valley town of stone cottages and newer estates.

housing: North Northamptonshire brings together Kettering, Corby, Wellingborough, Rushden and the towns and villages of the Nene valley. Private lets are often Victorian terraces built for the shoe industry in Kettering, Wellingborough and Rushden, new-town houses in Corby and new-build homes on the large urban extensions. The villages and Oundle have limestone and ironstone cottages, many listed.
checkinTips: Victorian shoe-town terraces in Kettering, Wellingborough and Rushden: photograph the rear yard, alley access, gutters and any damp in back kitchens.
1950s to 1970s new-town houses in Corby: photograph windows, flat-roof sections, cladding and any condensation or mould.
New-build homes at Priors Hall, Hanwood Park and Stanton Cross: record snagging marks, sealant and any cracks so they are noted before the tenancy.
Ironstone and limestone cottages in the villages and Oundle: record damp patches, flaking mortar and any wood burner and flue.
Homes near the River Nene: note any signs of past flooding on floors and lower walls.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair or safety concerns can contact North Northamptonshire Council's private sector housing team, which licenses HMOs and can inspect homes.
